title: On the Robustness of Sparse Randomized Sketching to FP16 Rounding on GPUs
summary: Randomized sketching replaces large matrices with smaller surrogates that preserve geometry for downstream numerical linear algebra. Sparse sketches promise faster formation than dense projections, but irregular GPU atomic updates become costly when each input row contributes to several output rows, as in SparseStack. FP16 accumulation halves sketch storage and update traffic, relieving cache pressure. How much does this rounding affect sketch geometry and downstream accuracy?
